# The Jesus Archive

> A free, ad-free reading room of every surviving witness to Jesus of Nazareth, each in its own words with sources: the Old Testament prophecies and the New Testament, Roman and Jewish writers (Tacitus, Josephus, Pliny, Suetonius, the Talmud), the early Church Fathers, archaeology (the Pilate stone, the Caiaphas ossuary, the Isaiah scroll), the other gospels, and the manuscript record.

## About
- [About The Jesus Archive](https://thejesusarchive.com/about): Who edits The Jesus Archive, how its sources are chosen and cited, and how to report an error. An independent, free archive with no ads or login.
- [Frequently Asked Questions](https://thejesusarchive.com/faq): Short, sourced answers to common questions about the historical Jesus: did he exist, what Roman and Jewish writers said, the Gospels, the manuscripts…

## Studies
- [Prophecy and Fulfilment](https://thejesusarchive.com/prophecies): Thirty-six passages from Israel’s scriptures set beside the New Testament scenes that read them as fulfilled in Jesus, from Bethlehem to the right hand of God.
- [The Resurrection](https://thejesusarchive.com/resurrection): Eight lines of evidence, drawn from the Gospels, Paul, Roman and Jewish writers and the first Christian leaders, set side by side for the reader to weigh.
- [How the Text Survived](https://thejesusarchive.com/manuscripts): No original of any New Testament book survives, but thousands of copies do, some within decades or a few generations of the writing, more than for any other…
- [The Life of Christ](https://thejesusarchive.com/life): The life of Jesus told in order, from the angel’s message in Nazareth to the empty tomb and Pentecost, each scene linked to the Gospels that tell it.
- [The Timeline](https://thejesusarchive.com/timeline): Every witness in this archive, placed in the order it was written or made: prophecy and Gospel, historian and Father, stone and scroll.
- [Start Here: Twelve Stops Through the Evidence](https://thejesusarchive.com/path): Twelve stops through the oldest evidence for Jesus of Nazareth, beginning with the earliest, written by those closest to him, and moving outward to Roman…

## The Prophets
- [The Prophets](https://thejesusarchive.com/old-testament): The chapters of the law, the psalms and the prophets that the first Christians read as pointing to Jesus, given in full so each promise can be read in its own…
- [Genesis: the call of Abraham](https://thejesusarchive.com/scripture/old-testament/genesis): The first book of the Torah. In chapter 12 God calls Abraham and promises that through him all the families of the earth will be blessed, a promise Paul read…
- [Exodus: the first Passover](https://thejesusarchive.com/scripture/old-testament/exodus): The second book of the Torah. Chapter 12 institutes the Passover, with its unblemished lamb whose blood marks the doors and whose bones are not to be broken…
- [Numbers: the bronze serpent and the star](https://thejesusarchive.com/scripture/old-testament/numbers): The fourth book of the Torah, following Israel through the wilderness. Chapter 21 tells of the bronze serpent lifted on a pole, and chapter 24 of Balaam’s…
- [2 Samuel: the promise to David](https://thejesusarchive.com/scripture/old-testament/2-samuel): The story of David’s reign, c. 1000 BC. In chapter 7 God promises David, through the prophet Nathan, a son and a throne established forever, the root of…
- [Psalms: the songs read of the Messiah](https://thejesusarchive.com/scripture/old-testament/psalms): Eight of Israel’s psalms that the New Testament reads as speaking of Jesus: royal songs of the king God enthrones, and laments of a righteous sufferer…
- [Isaiah: the chapters read as prophecy](https://thejesusarchive.com/scripture/old-testament/isaiah): The longest of the prophets, from Jerusalem in the eighth century BC. These chapters, from the sign of Immanuel to the suffering servant of chapter 53, are…
- [Jeremiah: Rachel’s weeping and the new covenant](https://thejesusarchive.com/scripture/old-testament/jeremiah): The prophet of Jerusalem’s last years before the Babylonian conquest. Chapter 31 holds Rachel weeping for her children and the promise of a new covenant…
- [Daniel: the vision of the Son of Man](https://thejesusarchive.com/scripture/old-testament/daniel): Visions of the empires and of God’s coming kingdom. In chapter 7 one like a son of man comes with the clouds to receive an everlasting dominion, the figure…
- [Hosea: out of Egypt I called my son](https://thejesusarchive.com/scripture/old-testament/hosea): A prophet of the northern kingdom in the eighth century BC. Chapter 11 remembers God calling Israel, his son, out of Egypt, a line Matthew applies to the…
- [Joel: the Spirit poured out](https://thejesusarchive.com/scripture/old-testament/joel): A prophet of the day of Yahweh. Chapter 2 promises that God will pour out his Spirit on all flesh, the passage Peter quoted at Pentecost.
- [Jonah: three days in the fish](https://thejesusarchive.com/scripture/old-testament/jonah): The story of a prophet who flees God’s call and is swallowed by a great fish for three days and three nights, the sign Jesus gave of his own death and rising.
- [Micah: the ruler from Bethlehem](https://thejesusarchive.com/scripture/old-testament/micah): A prophet of Judah in the late eighth century BC. Chapter 5 looks for a ruler of Israel from Bethlehem, David’s town, whose origins are from of old.
- [Zechariah: the humble king and the stricken shepherd](https://thejesusarchive.com/scripture/old-testament/zechariah): A prophet of the return from exile. These chapters, of the king riding on a donkey, the thirty pieces of silver, the one who was pierced and the shepherd…

## The New Testament

- [Paul's Letter to the Galatians](https://thejesusarchive.com/scripture/new-testament/09-galatians): Paul’s forceful letter to the churches of Galatia, from the late 40s or 50s AD. In it he tells, in the first person, how he stayed with Peter in Jerusalem and…
- [Paul's First Letter to the Corinthians](https://thejesusarchive.com/scripture/new-testament/07-1-corinthians): Paul’s letter to the church he founded in Corinth, c. AD 53–55. It preserves the earliest written account of the Lord’s Supper and, in 15:3–8, an older…
- [Paul's Second Letter to the Corinthians](https://thejesusarchive.com/scripture/new-testament/08-2-corinthians): Paul’s second surviving letter to Corinth, c. AD 55–56, written in a season of strain. It defends his apostleship and recalls his escape from Damascus under…
- [Paul's Letter to the Romans](https://thejesusarchive.com/scripture/new-testament/06-romans): Paul’s longest letter, written c. AD 55–58 to a church he had not yet visited. Its opening preserves what may be an older confession: Jesus born of David’s…
- [Paul's Letter to the Philippians](https://thejesusarchive.com/scripture/new-testament/11-philippians): Paul’s warm letter from prison to his first church in Europe. Its hymn to Christ (2:6–11), possibly older than Paul, shows that within about twenty-five years…
- [Paul's Letter to Philemon](https://thejesusarchive.com/scripture/new-testament/18-philemon): Paul’s shortest letter: a personal appeal from prison on behalf of Onesimus, an enslaved man who had become a believer, to be received as “a beloved brother”…
- [The Letter to the Colossians](https://thejesusarchive.com/scripture/new-testament/12-colossians): A letter of Paul and Timothy to the church at Colossae, received as Paul’s by Irenaeus and the early church. Its hymn-like passage (1:15–20) calls Christ “the…
- [The Letter to the Ephesians](https://thejesusarchive.com/scripture/new-testament/10-ephesians): A letter of Paul from prison on the unity of Jews and gentiles in Christ, received as his throughout the early church. It presents Christ as the one who…
- [The Second Letter to the Thessalonians](https://thejesusarchive.com/scripture/new-testament/14-2-thessalonians): Paul’s second letter to Thessalonica, received as his by Irenaeus and the early church. It answers a claim that “the day of Christ has already come”, evidence…
- [The First Letter to Timothy](https://thejesusarchive.com/scripture/new-testament/15-1-timothy): One of the Pastoral Letters, addressed in Paul’s name to his co-worker Timothy and quoted as Paul’s by Irenaeus. It contains a short hymn about Christ and…
- [The Second Letter to Timothy](https://thejesusarchive.com/scripture/new-testament/16-2-timothy): Presented as Paul’s last letter, written from prison as he faced death. Its summary of the gospel, “Jesus Christ, risen from the dead, of the offspring of…
- [The Letter to Titus](https://thejesusarchive.com/scripture/new-testament/17-titus): The third Pastoral Letter, addressed in Paul’s name to Titus, left in Crete to appoint elders. Mostly about church leadership, it looks for the appearing of…
- [The Gospel of Mark](https://thejesusarchive.com/scripture/new-testament/02-mark): The shortest Gospel, which the earliest tradition traces to Mark, the interpreter of Peter. Its fast-moving account of the ministry in Galilee and the passion…
- [The Gospel of Matthew](https://thejesusarchive.com/scripture/new-testament/01-matthew): The Gospel most read in the early church, attributed from the second century to Matthew the tax collector, one of the Twelve. It presents Jesus as Israel’s…
- [The Gospel of Luke](https://thejesusarchive.com/scripture/new-testament/03-luke): The first volume of Luke–Acts, attributed from the second century to Luke, the physician and companion of Paul. Its prologue describes its own method, drawing…
- [The Acts of the Apostles](https://thejesusarchive.com/scripture/new-testament/05-acts): The second volume of Luke–Acts, attributed from the second century to Luke, companion of Paul: the earliest narrative of the first Christian communities, from…
- [The Gospel of John](https://thejesusarchive.com/scripture/new-testament/04-john): The Fourth Gospel, which Irenaeus and the early church attributed to John the apostle, the “disciple whom Jesus loved”. Largely independent of the other…
- [The Letter to the Hebrews](https://thejesusarchive.com/scripture/new-testament/19-hebrews): An anonymous sermon in letter form, c. AD 60–90, which some early churches ascribed to Paul and Origen said only God knows who wrote. It presents Jesus as the…
- [The Letter of James](https://thejesusarchive.com/scripture/new-testament/20-james): A letter of moral teaching from “James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ”, traditionally the brother of Jesus and leader of the Jerusalem church…
- [The First Letter of Peter](https://thejesusarchive.com/scripture/new-testament/21-1-peter): A letter from “Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ” to Christians in Asia Minor facing hostility, used by Polycarp and accepted throughout the early church. Its…
- [The Second Letter of Peter](https://thejesusarchive.com/scripture/new-testament/22-2-peter): A testament in the name of Simon Peter, appealing to his presence at the transfiguration: “we were eyewitnesses of his majesty”. Slow to win acceptance and…
- [The First Letter of John](https://thejesusarchive.com/scripture/new-testament/23-1-john): A treatise from the circle of the beloved disciple, attributed from the second century to John the apostle. Written to a divided community, it proclaims what…
- [The Second Letter of John](https://thejesusarchive.com/scripture/new-testament/24-2-john): A brief letter from “the elder” to a congregation, which Irenaeus quotes as the work of John, the Lord’s disciple. It warns against deceivers who do not…
- [The Third Letter of John](https://thejesusarchive.com/scripture/new-testament/25-3-john): A private letter from “the elder” to Gaius about hospitality to travelling missionaries who went out “for the sake of the Name”. It does not name Jesus, but…
- [The Letter of Jude](https://thejesusarchive.com/scripture/new-testament/26-jude): A short, urgent letter from “Jude, a servant of Jesus Christ, and brother of James”, traditionally one of the brothers of Jesus. Accepted in the Muratorian…

## The Early Church
- [The Early Church](https://thejesusarchive.com/fathers): The generations after the apostles: their teaching, worship, arguments and memories, from the Didache to the first history of the Church.
- [The Didache (The Teaching of the Twelve Apostles)](https://thejesusarchive.com/fathers/didache): A short early church manual: the 'Two Ways' of life and death, then instructions on baptism, fasting, the Lord's Prayer, eucharistic prayers, travelling…
- [The First Epistle of Clement to the Corinthians](https://thejesusarchive.com/fathers/1-clement): A letter from the church at Rome to the church at Corinth, traditionally dated c. 96. It recalls the deaths of Peter and Paul, quotes sayings of Jesus, and…
- [Ignatius of Antioch, Letter to the Smyrnaeans](https://thejesusarchive.com/fathers/ignatius-smyrnaeans): Written by the bishop of Antioch on his way to execution in Rome. He insists that Jesus was truly born, truly nailed to the cross under Pontius Pilate and…
- [Papias of Hierapolis, Fragments](https://thejesusarchive.com/fathers/papias-fragments): Quotations from a lost early-2nd-century work by the bishop of Hierapolis, who sought out what followers of the apostles remembered. They include the earliest…
- [Justin Martyr, First Apology](https://thejesusarchive.com/fathers/justin-first-apology): A Christian philosopher's defence addressed to Antoninus Pius. It says Jesus was crucified under Pontius Pilate, argues from the Hebrew prophets, and gives…
- [Irenaeus of Lyons, Against Heresies, Book I](https://thejesusarchive.com/fathers/irenaeus-ah-1): Irenaeus sets out the 'Rule of Faith' the churches had received from the apostles and describes the Gnostic teachers he opposed, from Valentinus to Basilides…
- [Irenaeus of Lyons, Against Heresies, Book III](https://thejesusarchive.com/fathers/irenaeus-ah-3): The classic second-century defence of the four Gospels: how Matthew, Mark, Luke and John came to be written, why there are four and only four, and the…
- [Hippolytus, Refutation of All Heresies, Book IX](https://thejesusarchive.com/fathers/hippolytus-refutation-9): A Roman presbyter attacks teachers of his own day who said the Father and the Son were one and the same, including Bishop Callistus, and the Elchasaites. It…
- [Origen, Against Celsus, Book I](https://thejesusarchive.com/fathers/origen-contra-celsum-1): Origen replies to Celsus, a 2nd-century critic who called Jesus the son of a soldier named Panthera and a magician trained in Egypt. Along the way he cites…
- [Eusebius, Church History, Book I](https://thejesusarchive.com/fathers/eusebius-he-1): The opening book of the first history of the Church. It sets Jesus in the time of Augustus, Herod, Pilate and Caiaphas, quotes Josephus on John the Baptist…
- [Eusebius, Church History, Book III](https://thejesusarchive.com/fathers/eusebius-he-3): Eusebius on the generation after the apostles: the origins of the four Gospels, his list of accepted and disputed books, Papias on Mark and Matthew, Jesus's…
- [Eusebius, Church History, Book IV](https://thejesusarchive.com/fathers/eusebius-he-4): The second century, from Trajan to Marcus Aurelius: Quadratus's claim that people healed by Jesus lived into his own day, Hadrian's rescript, Justin Martyr…
- [Eusebius, Church History, Book V](https://thejesusarchive.com/fathers/eusebius-he-5): The late second century: the martyrs of Lyon and Vienne, Irenaeus on how the four Gospels were written, his memory of Polycarp and John, the Easter…
- [Athanasius of Alexandria, Festal Letter 39](https://thejesusarchive.com/fathers/athanasius-festal-39): The Easter letter of 367 in which the bishop of Alexandria lists the books of Scripture. It is the earliest surviving list of exactly the 27 books of today's…

## Stones and Scrolls
- [Stones and Scrolls](https://thejesusarchive.com/archaeology): Inscriptions, ossuaries, mosaics and scrolls. These are physical traces of the world Jesus lived in and of the first people who worshipped him.
- [The Great Isaiah Scroll (1QIsaᵃ)](https://thejesusarchive.com/archaeology/dead-sea-scrolls-isaiah): The only complete biblical book among the Dead Sea Scrolls, copied in the second century BC. It shows that Isaiah, a book Christians read as foretelling…
- [The Pilate inscription (Caesarea Maritima)](https://thejesusarchive.com/archaeology/pilate-inscription): A limestone block from Caesarea Maritima with a Latin dedication naming "Pontius Pilate, Prefect of Judea". It is the only contemporary inscription naming the…
- [The Caiaphas ossuary](https://thejesusarchive.com/archaeology/caiaphas-ossuary): An ornate limestone bone box from a first-century Jerusalem family tomb, inscribed "Joseph son of Caiaphas". Most scholars accept that it belonged to the…
- [The heel bone of Yehohanan (Giv’at HaMivtar)](https://thejesusarchive.com/archaeology/yehohanan-heel-bone): The right heel bone of a young Jewish man named Yehohanan, still pierced by the iron nail that fixed him to a cross. Found in a family tomb in Jerusalem in…
- [The Nazareth inscription](https://thejesusarchive.com/archaeology/nazareth-inscription): A Greek imperial edict on marble forbidding the disturbance of tombs, once linked to Jesus's empty tomb because it was "sent from Nazareth" in 1878. Isotope…
- [The Magdala Stone (Galilee)](https://thejesusarchive.com/archaeology/magdala-stone): A carved stone block found in 2009 at the centre of a first-century synagogue at Magdala, on the Sea of Galilee. Its seven-branched menorah, carved while the…
- [The Pool of Siloam (Jerusalem)](https://thejesusarchive.com/archaeology/pool-of-siloam): A large stepped pool at the southern end of ancient Jerusalem, discovered by chance in 2004. Built in the first century BC and used until the Roman…
- [The Pool of Bethesda (Jerusalem)](https://thejesusarchive.com/archaeology/pool-of-bethesda): Two large rock-cut basins north of the Temple Mount, in the grounds of the Church of St Anne in Jerusalem. Their layout, with a dividing wall between them…
- [The Gallio inscription (Delphi)](https://thejesusarchive.com/archaeology/gallio-inscription): Fragments of a letter from the emperor Claudius, carved on stone at Delphi in Greece, naming Gallio as proconsul of Achaia. Dated by Claudius’s titles to AD…
- [The James ossuary (disputed)](https://thejesusarchive.com/archaeology/james-ossuary): A limestone bone box inscribed "James, son of Joseph, brother of Jesus", announced in 2002 without an excavation record. Experts still debate whether the…
- [The Alexamenos graffito (Palatine, Rome)](https://thejesusarchive.com/archaeology/alexamenos-graffito): A crude drawing scratched into plaster on the Palatine Hill in Rome: a man raises his hand to a crucified figure with a donkey’s head, above the Greek words…
- [The Megiddo mosaic ("God Jesus Christ")](https://thejesusarchive.com/archaeology/megiddo-mosaic): A third-century mosaic floor from a Christian prayer hall near Megiddo, found in 2005, with a Greek dedication "to God Jesus Christ". It is among the earliest…
- [The Christian building at Dura-Europos](https://thejesusarchive.com/archaeology/dura-europos-christian-building): A private house on the Euphrates remodelled for Christian worship, with a baptistery painted with scenes of Christ healing and the women at the tomb. Sealed…
- [The Frankfurt silver amulet (Nida)](https://thejesusarchive.com/archaeology/frankfurt-silver-amulet): A rolled silver amulet from a third-century grave at Roman Nida (Frankfurt), read by CT scanning in 2024. Its text invokes Jesus, making it among the earliest…

## The Other Gospels

- [Q: The Sayings Source (a Scholarly Reconstruction)](https://thejesusarchive.com/gospels/q-sayings-source): Q is a hypothetical sayings source that, on the two-source theory, Matthew and Luke used alongside Mark. No manuscript exists; this is a modern reconstruction…
- [Sayings of Jesus (Papyrus Oxyrhynchus 5575)](https://thejesusarchive.com/gospels/sayings-of-jesus-p-oxy-5575): A small second-century papyrus, published in 2023, preserving sayings of Jesus close to Matthew 6, Luke 12 and the Gospel of Thomas: on anxiety, the birds and…
- [The Egerton Gospel (Papyrus Egerton 2)](https://thejesusarchive.com/gospels/egerton-gospel): Fragments of an unknown second-century gospel on papyrus: Jesus tells the rulers to search the scriptures, escapes arrest, heals a leper and answers a…
- [The Stranger’s Book (Allogenes, Codex Tchacos)](https://thejesusarchive.com/gospels/strangers-book): A damaged Sethian text from Codex Tchacos whose hero, “Stranger”, is tempted by Satan, transfigured in a bright cloud on Mount Tabor and taught to ascend past…
- [The Secret Gospel of Mark (the Mar Saba Letter)](https://thejesusarchive.com/gospels/secret-gospel-of-mark): A letter ascribed to Clement of Alexandria, reported by Morton Smith in 1958, that quotes a “more spiritual” expanded Gospel of Mark. The manuscript cannot…
- [The Infancy Gospel of James (Protevangelium of James)](https://thejesusarchive.com/gospels/infancy-gospel-of-james): A second-century legend of Mary’s birth, childhood and virginity, ending with Jesus’s birth in a cave near Bethlehem. Not a historical source, but enormously…
- [The Infancy Gospel of Thomas](https://thejesusarchive.com/gospels/infancy-gospel-of-thomas): Legends of Jesus between five and twelve: clay sparrows that fly, curses and healings, and lessons that confound his teachers. A second-century story cycle…
- [The Gospel of Peter (Akhmim Fragment)](https://thejesusarchive.com/gospels/gospel-of-peter): A second-century Passion and resurrection narrative told in Peter’s name, known from an Egyptian manuscript found in 1886–87. It retells the canonical story…
- [The Gospel of Nicodemus (Acts of Pilate) and the Pilate Letters](https://thejesusarchive.com/gospels/apocryphal-gospels-anf08-walker-1870): Late-antique Christian legends of Jesus’s trial before Pilate, his descent into Hades, and letters in Pilate’s name, from the Ante-Nicene Fathers. Not Roman…
- [The Gospel of Mary](https://thejesusarchive.com/gospels/gospel-of-mary): A fragmentary second-century dialogue in which the risen Savior teaches and departs, Mary relates a vision of the soul’s ascent, and Peter and Andrew dispute…
- [The Gospel of Judas](https://thejesusarchive.com/gospels/gospel-of-judas): A second-century revelation dialogue, known to Irenaeus and recovered in Coptic in Codex Tchacos, in which Jesus mocks the disciples’ worship and gives Judas…
- [The Gospel of Philip](https://thejesusarchive.com/gospels/gospel-of-philip): A Valentinian anthology of sayings and reflections on baptism, anointing, the Eucharist and the bridal chamber, preserved at Nag Hammadi. Often…
- [The Gospel of Truth](https://thejesusarchive.com/gospels/gospel-of-truth): A second-century Valentinian meditation on how Jesus, “nailed to a tree”, made known the unknown Father and dispelled ignorance. Probably the work Irenaeus…
- [The Secret Book of James (Apocryphon of James)](https://thejesusarchive.com/gospels/secret-book-of-james): A second-century letter in James’s name relating secret teaching of the risen Savior to James and Peter before his ascension: be “filled”, seek suffering…
- [Pistis Sophia](https://thejesusarchive.com/gospels/gutenberg/pistis-sophia-horner-1924): A Coptic Gnostic work in which the risen Jesus, eleven years after the resurrection, ascends in light, returns and teaches the disciples, Mary above all…
- [G. R. S. Mead, The Gnostic Crucifixion (1907)](https://thejesusarchive.com/gospels/gutenberg/gnostic-crucifixion-mead-1907): A 1907 theosophical study by G. R. S. Mead of the Vision of the Cross in the Acts of John, where the Lord tells John on the Mount of Olives that he did not…
